quotes.text: Accept Bacs Direct Debit payments from customers with a UK bank account.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Bacs Direct Debit payments must be in GBP.
However, Bacs Direct Debit is a delayed notification payment method, which means that funds aren’t immediately available.
The Bacs Direct Debit scheme rules require that your customer accept a mandate in order for Stripe to debit their account.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/bacs-debit/accept-a-payment, the complete November capture establishes only that Bacs Direct Debit accepts payments from customers with UK bank accounts and routes readers to Checkout and Elements variants (new raw lines 5-14). The May 2 guide supplies the dated details: Checkout uses a GBP Product/Price and server-created payment-mode Session with Bacs selection; checkout.session.completed means debit authorization, while async_payment_succeeded means later success and async_payment_failed means failure (old raw lines 16-28, 79-90, 93-168). The Elements path collects mandate acknowledgement, creates a GBP PaymentIntent server-side for Customer or qualified customer-configured Account, submits Elements and confirms client-side; payment_intent.succeeded, processing and payment_failed are distinct (old raw lines 326-371, 575-709, 703-769, 852-877). Accounts v2 was GA for Connect and preview for others with preview-version requirement (old raw lines 8-14). source-stripe-bacs-accept-payment.md already states the Checkout authorization/async-success boundary at line 21; its remaining gaps are dated provenance, labeling setup_future_usage off_session as optional save-for-later, success_url reliability, delayed funds, and eligibility qualifications (current source lines 1-30, 32-65). The related concept likewise needs the optional-save qualification at line 82. Session creation, mandate authorization and browser return are not payment success or funds availability.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/bacs-debit/accept-a-payment, the November change is presentation and variant navigation: the combined guide was replaced by Checkout and Elements links, with no demonstrated substantive change to payment rules (new raw lines 7-14; old raw lines 16-28, 326-332; diff lines 1-29, 1060-1062). source-stripe-bacs-accept-payment.md must retain the May 2, 2026 Checkout/Elements, sandbox test, optional target_date and mandate-prefix claims as dated, add canonical_url and both raw routes, and narrow its unsupported 'succeeds immediately' sandbox timing and incomplete prefix rule (current source lines 1-9, 17-22, 32-65; old raw lines 276-324, 887-956). Both source line 20 and concept stripe-bacs-direct-debit.md line 82 should qualify setup_future_usage off_session as an optional save-for-later example (old raw lines 116-139); source line 21 already correctly separates mandate authorization from async success. The old Checkout prose says funds typically available in three business days, but Elements describes T+4 availability and 4/7-day confirmation; this needs route-specific dated wording, not one universal promise (old raw lines 158, 858-870). Checkout Session completion/redirect means authorization or details collected, while async success and PaymentIntent succeeded are later payment states; neither equates to available funds (old raw lines 112-174, 852-877). Customer versus Accounts v2 access, GBP/UK scope, Checkout versus web Elements, and sandbox-only results all remain qualified; the index does not renew current detailed behavior (new raw lines 9-14).
